subject: Renewal: safety-net commit uplift and credit exchange
messages:
From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>
To: Lisa Chen <lisa@brightware.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 14 Apr 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Renewal: safety-net commit uplift and credit exchange

Hi Lisa —

Congrats again on the volume growth over Q1. As your renewal window approaches (contract ends 2027-06-30), we wanted to propose a structure that protects BrightWare from unexpected overages while keeping your unit economics stable as you scale. High level idea:

- Safety-net uplift: BrightWare commits to a stepped uplift (10% in Q3, 15% in Q4) across token commitments to lock current per-token pricing for 12 months.
- Bridge credit: In exchange, Redwood provides a one-time credit pool you can draw against for burst capacity (applies only to overage in excess of 120% of committed volume).
- True-up cadence: Quarterly true-ups with a 30-day notice window for major usage shifts.

Can you share an updated forecast for June–Dec (rough buckets OK)? Attached is the Q1 usage export we pulled to seed the discussion.

If this looks promising, we can circulate a short amendment and a simple mutual action plan.

Thanks,
Hannah
Hannah Schmitt
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

From: Lisa Chen <lisa@brightware.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>
Cc: Procurements <procure@brightware.com>, Daniel Park <daniel.park@brightware.com>
Date: Wed, 14 Apr 2027 12:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Renewal: safety-net commit uplift and credit exchange

Hi Hannah —

Thanks for the clear proposal. High level reactions from our side:

- We like the idea of preserving price while we scale, but need a cap on the total commit uplift if our growth underperforms.
- The burst credit feature is useful — can credits be used across projects (we have two product lines using Redwood)?
- Procurement will want clarity on billing mechanics and any clawback language.

I'll pull a quick forecast for June–Dec and loop in Procurement. One ask: can we get a sample amendment so our legal/procurement can review concurrently?

Best,
Lisa
Lisa Chen
Head of Platform, BrightWare
lisa@brightware.com
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 15 Apr 2027 08:21:00 -07:00
Subject: RE: Renewal: safety-net commit uplift and credit exchange

Looping in Karthik for pricing/legal guardrails. A few quick internal notes before we send an amendment:

- Recommend a two-way floor: if BrightWare underdelivers <90% of uplifted commit over a 6-month window, we recover a pro-rated portion of the credit (clawback) — but cap the recovery at 25% of the credit pool.
- Credits should be org-wide but tagged per project for accounting; allow a single drawdown per billing period.
- Keep the price-hold term to 12 months and allow a one-time rollover if both sides agree.

I can draft a short amendment skeleton for Hannah to push to Lisa.
Ben
Ben Carter
Sr. Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference
From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>
To: Lisa Chen <lisa@brightware.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 15 Apr 2027 11:47:00 -07:00
Subject: RE: Renewal: safety-net commit uplift and credit exchange

Lisa —

Appreciate the quick feedback. Attached is draft-amendment-v2.pdf (skeleton amendment — legal-friendly version of the bullets below). Key points called out in the doc:

- Commit ladder: Q3 +10%, Q4 +15% (applies to baseline token commitment in current agreement).
- Burst credit: $60k credit pool, org-scoped, drawn per billing period, expires 12 months after renewal effective date.
- Clawback: 6-month measurement window, recovery only if actuals <90% of uplifted commit, capped at 25% credit recovery.
- Price hold: existing per-token rates preserved for 12 months post-renewal; if usage grows >200% we reserve right to reprice newly added volume after notice.

If the economics look favorable to Lisa, we'll ask procurement for a short SOW with billing contacts and then route the amendment for signature.

Hannah

Attachment: draft-amendment-v2.pdf
From: Daniel Park <daniel.park@brightware.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>, Lisa Chen <lisa@brightware.com>
Cc: Procurements <procure@brightware.com>
Date: Fri, 16 Apr 2027 16:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Renewal: safety-net commit uplift and credit exchange

Hannah / Lisa —

Quick note from procurement after a fast review: two asks before we can sign off to legal review:

1) Can the credit pool be converted to a multi-month amortized credit instead of a single draw? That helps our internal budget planning.
2) We need clear examples in the amendment showing how a clawback calculation works (sample math).

If you can include a one-paragraph sample amortization schedule and a worked example of the 25% clawback cap, we can route to legal next week.

Thanks,
Daniel Park
Sourcing Manager, BrightWare
procure@brightware.com
